title: copier: put: resolve symlinks before os.Root path check
body:
os.Root.Lstat rejects absolute symlinks (e.g. /var/run -> /run) even when the target stays inside the container root.  Resolve paths with chroot-like semantics before the os.Root check so that in-container absolute symlinks no longer cause "path escapes from parent" errors. Relative symlink escapes (e.g. symlink -> ..) are rejected, matching Docker behavior (moby/go-archive#93).

Fixes: https://github.com/podman-container-tools/podman/issues/29805

comments.body: Also I think it would be a good idea for any code that could possibly change the destination filesystem to have unit tests covering ~every single case. (All the more a reason to factor out the moby/go-archive error compatibility in to a read-only helper which would not, so urgently, need such detailed testing.)
@mtrmac I have addressed the review. I reworked the whole PR. I literally missed handling the relative symlinks.
I am not fully sure about this behavior change. The `resolvePath` caps `..` at root (matching real chroot semantics), which is safe but differs from Docker.

I have addressed simple nonblocking comments about testing. 

---

Note: Docker fixed the same issue in [moby/go-archive#93](https://github.com/moby/go-archive/pull/93) with the same approach. Resolve absolute symlinks relative to extraction root before `os.Root`. The only difference is `..` symlinks: Docker rejects them; buildah's `resolvePath` caps them at root (chroot semantics). That's the `add-parent-symlink` conformance skip.

---

Since this is a regression that impacts users. Please review and merge @podman-container-tools/podman-maintainers @podman-container-tools/buildah-maintainers @nalind @mtrmac @mheon @Luap99. Thanks in advance.
